chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, who said, 'I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him)'; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who both said, 'We asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him)'

about a man who bequeathed a 'portion' (sahm) from his wealth, and we do not know what this 'portion' is. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there not with you, among what has reached you from Ja'far (peace be upon him) nor from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), anything regarding it?' We said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! We have not heard our companions mentioning anything of this from your forefathers (peace be upon him).'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The 'portion' is one from eight.' So we said to him (peace be upon him), 'May we be sacrificed for you! How did it become one from eight?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not read the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I do read it, but I do not know which place it is.'

The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials appointed over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer.'

Then he (peace be upon him) made (the number) eight with his hand, and said: 'And similarly, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it upon eight portions. Therefore, the 'portion' is one from eight.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'portion' (sahm) in Islamic bequests according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) resolves the ambiguity of a bequest specifying only a 'portion' by defining it as one of the eight categories of zakat recipients mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah. He establishes this by citing the Quranic verse and demonstrating how the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) historically divided wealth into these eight equal shares, thereby providing a clear jurisprudential precedent for inheritance and charity distribution in Shia fiqh.
